Which companies worry about tariffs on i.answer: Several companies that the search surfaced name China specifically in their tariff risks. Intuitive Surgical says tariffs and U.S.-China tensions could raise its costs and reduce demand [1][2]. Boeing notes that Chinese customers paused deliveries in 2025 amid tariff talks [3]. Apple cites new tariffs on imports from mainland China [4], and Amgen warns that Section 301 tariffs on Chinese goods could hit pharmaceutical inputs [5]. Eli Lilly says it depends on China-based suppliers and that new U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods were imposed in 2025 [6][7]. Tesla and Deere raise tariff concerns more broadly, with Tesla noting uncertainty over China trade agreements [8]. Across the 102 companies, 61 added or expanded tariff and trade language this year, and 5 cut it [9]. The filings excerpts do not give a complete list of every company that mentions China tariffs, so this is a sample rather than an exhaustive count.

How does JPMorgan describe the risk of a.answer: JPMorgan treats cyberattacks as a major operational risk, and its main cyber risk factor is titled "A successful cyber attack could cause significant harm to JPMorganChase and its clients and customers." The filing says it could become "increasingly vulnerable to cyber attacks" if it does not promptly fix known weaknesses, such as zero-day vulnerabilities and weak access controls [1][2]. It also flags risks from outside parties: failures or attacks on third-party systems, retailers, payment processors and cloud services could disrupt its operations [3][4]. The filing describes this risk as rewritten this year, and it cites defenses such as protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks and ransomware [5].

Which companies stopped mentioning ESG?.answer: 26 of the 102 companies dropped ESG language from their risk factors entirely this year, out of 53 that used it last year [1]. They are Adobe, Amgen, American Tower, Broadcom, American Express, Booking Holdings, Comcast, Salesforce, GE Aerospace, Gilead Sciences, Goldman Sachs, Intel, Intuit, JPMorgan Chase, Mondelez International, MetLife, ServiceNow, Procter & Gamble, Qualcomm, RTX, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Tesla, Texas Instruments, U.S. Bancorp, Wells Fargo, and Walmart [1]. A further 34 companies still mention ESG but use it less often [1]. One example of removed wording is Adobe's line that "Laws, regulations and policies relating to environmental, social, and governance are expanding globally" [2].
